about: The one-byte patch the launch agent (agent/launch.ts) makes in memory when the game maps GameAssembly.dll, so the command-line player loader builds a human player and not the bot. The agent holds no address or byte of its own: this whole file rides in its arm message. It writes only when the loader's first bytes and the patch site both read as listed here, and the game file on disk is never written. launch selects how bot_run starts the game and defer whether the patch waits for setImmediate; the plan is docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-31-ch-mcp-direct-start.md (removed; git show 6804353f:docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-31-ch-mcp-direct-start.md), "The launch" and question 1. The loader's facts are on docs/clone-hero/07-internals.md.

song_speed.about: Where the launch agent finds the game's song_speed setting and what it must hold before the one call above sets it, on the loader's first run, only when ch_start armed a speed. The object is static +0x10 of the class whose TypeInfo slot is at typeinfo_rva, with its statics at +0xB8 (docs/clone-hero/code/6142/settings_load_374D50.asm lines 2028 to 2030); the value, minimum and maximum are at +0x10, +0x14 and +0x18 (int_setting_clamp_FE5B10.asm lines 15 to 17); min and max are the limits the setting is built with (settings_load_374D50.asm lines 2020 to 2025, TM-59 on docs/clone-hero/03-timing.md). ch_start refuses a speed outside min and max before anything runs, and the agent refuses an object whose own limits differ. The setter stores the value and clamps it (int_setting_set_FE5F50.asm); its third argument is never read, so the agent passes null.
